cards: Tacitus was a Roman historian and senator of the late first and early second centuries CE, author of the Annals, the Histories and other works.
Jesus of Nazareth was a Jewish preacher from Galilee whose life and teaching are the basis of Christianity.
c. 4 BCE – c. 30/33 CE · Ancient Near East
Claudius was Roman emperor from 41 to 54 CE, proclaimed by the Praetorian Guard after the murder of his nephew Caligula.
Pliny the Elder was a Roman officer and writer whose Natural History, in 37 books, gathered knowledge of geography, peoples, animals, plants and minerals.
Plutarch was a Greek writer and philosopher from Chaeronea in Boeotia, who also served as a priest at Delphi.
Nero was Roman emperor from 54 to 68 CE, the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, adopted heir of Claudius.
Flavius Josephus was a Jewish historian and a former commander in the revolt against Rome.
Gnaeus Julius Agricola was a Roman general and governor of Britain from about 77 to 84 CE.
Caligula, properly Gaius Caesar, was Roman emperor from 37 to 41 CE, the son of Germanicus and successor of Tiberius.
Domitian was Roman emperor from 81 to 96 CE, the last of the Flavian dynasty.
Boudica was queen of the Iceni of eastern Britain who led a great revolt against Roman rule in 60 or 61 CE after the Romans seized her late husband's kingdom and mistreated her family.
Caratacus was a British chieftain, son of Cunobelinus of the Catuvellauni, who led resistance to the Roman invasion of 43 CE.
Cunobelinus was a king of the Catuvellauni who ruled much of south-eastern Britain from about 9 to 40 CE from his capital at Camulodunum, modern Colchester.
Germanicus Julius Caesar (15 BCE–19 CE) was a Roman general, nephew and adopted son of the emperor Tiberius.
Aulus Plautius was a Roman senator and general who commanded the invasion of Britain ordered by the emperor Claudius in 43 CE.
Ban Chao was a general of the Eastern Han dynasty who brought the city-states of the Tarim Basin back under Chinese control.
Gaius Suetonius Paulinus was a Roman general and governor of Britain from about 58 to 61 CE.
Gondophares was the founder of the Indo-Parthian Kingdom, ruling in the early 1st century CE over Sistan, Arachosia, Gandhara and Taxila, which he took from the Indo-Scythians.
r. c. 19–46 CE · Central & East Asia
Mark the Evangelist is the traditional author of the Gospel of Mark and, by Christian tradition, founder of the church of Alexandria.
Cartimandua was queen of the Brigantes of northern Britain in the 1st century CE and a client ruler of Rome.
Decebalus was king of Dacia from 87 to 106 CE.
Herod Agrippa I was a grandson of Herod the Great, raised in Rome and a friend of the emperors Caligula and Claudius.
c. 11 BCE–44 CE · Ancient Near East
John the Baptist was a Jewish preacher active in the Jordan valley in the early 1st century CE, who called for repentance and baptised followers in the river, among them Jesus.
Otho (Marcus Salvius Otho) was Roman emperor for three months in 69 CE, the Year of the Four Emperors.
Rhoemetalces III was the last king of Thrace, a Roman client ruler of the Sapaean house.
Silius Italicus was a Roman senator and poet, consul in 68 CE, who wrote the Punica, an epic in seventeen books on the Second Punic War and the longest surviving Latin poem.
Tacfarinas was a Numidian of the Musulamii who had served in the Roman auxiliary army and from 17 CE led a revolt against Rome in North Africa.
Titus was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 CE, the elder son of Vespasian and the second emperor of the Flavian dynasty.
Charibael was a king of the Himyarites and Sabaeans in south Arabia in the 1st century CE, known from the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.

Hero of Alexandria was a Greek mathematician and engineer who worked in Alexandria in the first century CE.
fl. 1st century CE · Egypt & North Africa
Julius Maternus was a Roman traveller who, according to Ptolemy's Geography citing Marinus of Tyre, journeyed with the king of the Garamantes on an expedition south from the Fezzan to the land of…
late 1st century CE · Egypt & North Africa
Pedanius Dioscorides was a Greek physician from Anazarbus in Cilicia who served with the Roman army.
Philo of Alexandria was a Jewish philosopher who lived in Alexandria and wrote in Greek.
c. 20 BCE–c. 50 CE · Ancient Near East
Pliny the Younger was a Roman lawyer, senator and author, nephew and adopted son of Pliny the Elder.
Poppaea Sabina was a Roman noblewoman, wife of Otho and then, from 62 CE, of the emperor Nero.
Publius Ostorius Scapula was Roman governor of Britain from 47 to 52.
Quintus Curtius Rufus was a Roman historian, probably of the 1st century CE, author of the Histories of Alexander the Great in ten books, of which the first two are lost.
Rhadamistus was an Iberian prince, son of King Pharasmanes I, who seized the kingdom of Armenia in 51 CE after treacherously killing his uncle Mithridates, its Roman-backed king.
d. c. 58 CE · Ancient Near East
